title: approval report
source: notes warrant-layer/benchmark-design.md §1, A2 (2026-11-25); GR3 at 10,000 (R311 kept, PLAN-v3-bench Decisions)
output: Per turn, a design: the components, the rules each rests on, the SQL per component, and caveats.

turns.text: Build a report for procurement: who can approve which requests, and why requests are not approved.
turns.example: As a worked example, give each component's figures for the pending requests of cost centre cc0049 and its subtree.

turns.text: Show the requests nobody can approve.
Break the not-approved requests down by reason, and show how long they have been waiting.
Show it as it stood at the end of July 2026.
turns.example: Give the approval limit of a manager, the register status of vendor bolt, and the cost centre of employee e077 as they stood then.

gold.text: An approver is anyone in the requester's reporting chain with a high enough limit, not only the direct manager
The limit that counts is the version valid on the request date; a later limit change does not reclassify old requests
Software requests under 10,000 are approved automatically, without an approver: a separate path, not attributed to anyone
Approved means eligible (approver, cap check, vendor check) and not denied; reasons co-occur, so a breakdown allows several reasons per request, not one bucket
Denied (a recorded policy violation, owned by compliance) is a different reason from not eligible (procurement, finance)
A request both denied and auto-approved is a conflict: show it as contested, in neither column
A cap failure may come from an ancestor centre's cap, not the requester's own
Vendor check on the request date; emergency requests pass despite a suspended vendor, except big capital requests (R307 overrides the waiver)
The reporting chain depends on where the requester sits on the request date (e077 moved; hr and finance disagree, finance prevails)
"How long waiting" is not defined by any rule (no SLA, no start event): ask, or state the assumption; do not invent one silently
"Nobody can approve" is a negative answer over known facts (chains and limits are not declared complete): label it
Period-end view needs "as of" throughout (limits, vendor status, chain), not today's data filtered by date
